Heya Jelly, 
We are referring to a timeline of feb-12-2022 to feb-12-2023. 
When we say EOY (End of Year) we are saying 'calendar year' to allow us for eval. of the fund results. 
Audit trail - native ecosystem assets with a multisig wallet can be tracked, out of ecosystem assets will be tied to wallets that are not native, but as we will be submitting monthly reports on this, there is community transparency for understanding asset allocation + valuation. 

I love the idea of tools to better manage / view allocations, so if you come up with something like that we would love to see how it would work and give it a trial run.

Oh, and I assume the audit trail will be pretty limited, so it's mostly "on trust"?  This is actually an area that would probably benefit from some tool development (not suggesting this is part of the current proposal).

I share some of Rich's concerns about this - plus that the amount to funds involved might actually be too little to maintain interest of the fund managers, but I'm willing to support the experiment.  Could I ask for a couple of clarifications though please, both to avoid future arguments?

> Timeline: 2-12-22 to 2-12-23

I assume this is Feb 12 2022 to Feb 12 2023?  Could we have an unambiguous date format please?

And references to "End of Year" - could you clarify whether that's end of timeline period or end of calendar year please?

The treasury proposal (#54) to fund the Asset Diversification experiment is now live, currently in the council motion stage (#78) to become a SimpleMajority referendum (likely to become a referendum in ~3-5 days).

**Just a clarification regarding the historical risk/reward calculations**
(from the original diversification post in DAO Financial Megathread)
> The data we used for these models is from Jan 2020 to Dec 2021 (based on when these coins came into existence) so as to get a mix of up-trends as well as the downtrends in the cryptocurrency markets. Also, we have taken the monthly averages of the prices for each token and their corresponding % changes.

Hiya Rich, 

Thank you for the feedback and the thoughts. 
As the fund starts to do better and if the model proves successful enough to scale, we can look towards creating the appropriate technical infrastructure to better support the 'on-chain treasury'. 

Of course, we appreciate feedback from the community and do believe that this is in line w/ the value of Edg and its community members, we just happen to be taking on and advisory role to help better allocate funds for future growth of members, the community as a whole and projects / teams seeking to build on these values.

1. are you asking in an operations perspective - as in how multisig wallets work to hold assets for each token? 
2. in terms of signers to the multisig it would be the team where 2-3 is require to take action w/ the funds in investing / divesting assets. ultimately we are a distributed trust systems industry, in this case we are distributing trust across 4 individuals whom have demonstrated involvement and contributions to the community in helping further this experiment as a DAO but also in delivering on financial tasks. 
3. historical data - as you know the industry is relatively young and some assets even more so. polkadot obviously doesnt have as much price data as bitcoin does - hence if using this logic we would never put funds in any other assets outside of BTC, so the modeling showing the best avail. price data based on the prelim. tasking
4. also to be clear we are not giving personal investment advice to you or the community. the funds requested are to be allocated such that we maximize profits for the fund as an experiment and any alpha generated to be used appropriately based on time horizon indicated above (details outlined in proposal above).
5. on value based investing - historical data along with the current monetary price is the way to find intrinsic value, that is in comparison to the underlying utilitarian value of the token in the network and the use-case of the protocol / blockchain. for example: 
6. kabocha's monetary value is non-existent due to a lack of historical data + no price discovery being displayed across cex's / dex's / 3rd party community markets. its utility value in the token is determined by the use-case that is there. 


Ultimately the idea is to invest / stake in people and the experiment that is the proposal is that if it proves to be successful in garnering knowledge to the members + the community and if any monetary value is accrued higher than the initial proposal request we as a community can decide how to best apply those

Thanks for the response [@ash|inthewild](/edgeware/account/nT3foVZGs2JSEQtoehuJn7F1U9okugnhwdqQTUgLMcQDxaj).

1. There is a very simple issue at the heart of the proposal: 


- The stated aim is for EDG treasury to invest in an exeperimental contributor run fund to speculate on the market and to learn about trading etc.
- 
- The hope is to create some extra funds which are to be directed back to the treasury to build a diversified portfolio and therefore decrease EDG volatility over time by making it 'asset backed' and / or help with issues like market making.


- However the EDG treasury literally cannot hold the funds you identify, only EDG itself. In the immediate future it will only be able to hold and govern Substrate assets (fungible / non fungible). 


- If you want to hold BTC/ETH or USDT/USDC then this will not be held on-chain, but instead managed by the contributors - therefore this is not backing the chain's treasury. 


- It might seem like semantics, but this is an important point if you are hoping to create a narrative or story that EDG has a diverse treasury. It doesn't and it won't, these are delegated funds, held by contributors. 


- There is a further problem with the EVM / ETH bridge approach - this model is a security nightmare and ultimately the approach of locking on one chain and then minting on another requires a 3rd party. [See Vitalik tweet. ]( https://twitter.com/VitalikButerin/status/1479501366192132099?s=20&t=GJ6KpjEKs6mYwym8rq63dQ)So when people say we should do this because all DAOs do, the reference is to ETH based DAOs, where their balance sheet is holding only ETH based assets such as USDT. 


- I constantly come back to this, but the whole reason Substrate  / relay chains were created was to enable interoperability between chains that spoke the same language and therefore removed this issue. As a result I still see this as a backwards step rather than one that embraces a true multichain future.

Kabocha is the first move to enabling Edgeware to build a diversified on-chain tresury made up of fungible and non-fungible tokens. It does this and also adds extra utility to the project. 

> Ultimately the idea is to invest / stake in people and the experiment that is the proposal is that if it proves to be successful in garnering knowledge to the members

My reservations remain on this proposal, but in the end the great thing about Edgeware is we develop people and projects in public where open and honest debates are vital since that's the only way things improve. It might seem slow, but that is by design. This is what decentralisation does...

Please appreciate this is just about the content of the proposal, not a lack of desire to fund your group.

Best of luck.

3. In terms of market making - this requires considerable resources even on an institutional level, that is not only in education but level of expertise and adequate financial incentives in deploying a team to doing this successfully. On Rich's negative points: 
1. Its not about being an 'and 1' or a 'they too", this method of diversification by creating a portfolio of assets outside of EDG is a tried and proven methodology for accruing monetary value in the Edg Treasury. Its the point a to b route that would allow us to keep the 'merry go round, merry and going round' 
2. the risk categories are simplified allocation of assets for user facing discussion. it gets too in the weeds w/ financial jargon, strategy and allocation reasoning. The assets in each category however are backed by both historical mkt trends and supplemental data which tracks marketing + technical + financial factors.
3. Day trading / algo's / 'edge' trading requires a 24/7-365 day commitment, which would require the team to be compensated accordingly, w/ no real guarantee of accruing positive returns in the end of the year (only 1% of day traders are really proffitable in tradefi - in crypto the #'s are much lower). - On creating and deploying an algo, Ash has actually created an algo that was back tested and deployed to Gate, however the returns were only around 4-5% making it not worth the overall allocation of time + potential profit. Trading algo's require a substantial amount of time to tool to really yield profits and ultimately dont work very well in the end of the day. 

Hence, the diversification approach along with managing the funds through a year's period in which it creates monetary value + network utility value (in specific. token cases) is the wisest strategy.

On Kosturp's comments: 
Stable-coins are great to keep a small basket of coins in, however our approach is to generate returns higher then that of the 10-12% returns stable-coins would yield. Our hypothesis is that the assets we are evaluating and creating investments in, will appreciate in value and create additional returns through staking that exceed that of stablecoins. 

'Gambling' and 'investing' on the surface sound / look the same but a critical difference is that is in this case the market (all the crypto tokens collectively) do not have an 'edge' against an investor. In gambling the 'edge' is held by the 'house' (casino) such that they created games that increases their probability of profit taking (from users) while maintaining a level of risk that creates an overall net positive for them.
This may be a bit of a simplified and esoteric explanation of the 2 concepts, but just figured it was the easiest to package and share :)
